result.title: LeanWAM: Learning Latent World Action Models from Frozen Video Models
result.summary: World action models (WAMs) typically adapt large pretrained video generators to jointly predict future observations and robot actions, incurring substantial training and deployment costs. However, it remains unclear which future representations a policy actually needs and how compactly they can be represented. Our probing study shows that complementary future representations can be compressed into a few tokens while retaining most of their action-decoding performance. Motivated by this finding, we introduce LeanWAM, a latent WAM that transfers video priors from a frozen video generator to a lightweight policy via two-stage training. In the first stage, a Future Extractor compresses observed transitions into 32 predictive tokens. These tokens condition the frozen generator and are jointly shaped by action, RGB, semantic, and geometric supervision, while a compact readout of the generator's hidden states supplies complementary world tokens. The second stage distills both representations into the policy, which learns to predict them from current observations while generating actions. With 1.4B parameters and no large-scale embodied pretraining, LeanWAM outperforms strong vision-language-action (VLA) and WAM baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin~2.0. It predicts an action chunk in 25.1\,ms on an A100 GPU, 12.3--41.5$\times$ faster than representative WAMs. These results demonstrate that compact predictive supervision can transfer video priors to robust and efficient control.

AI.brief_summary: LeanWAM 研究机器人策略需要何种未来表示，发现互补的未来表示可压缩为少量 token 而基本保留动作解码能力，据此用冻结视频生成器提供先验：第一阶段由 Future Extractor 将观测转移压成 32 个预测 token 并读取生成器隐状态作为世界 token，第二阶段蒸馏进轻量策略，实现毫秒级动作块预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「未来表示可压缩为极少量 token 且不损失下游解码」的探测结论与「冻结生成器隐状态读出＋蒸馏监督」流程，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的表示压缩、任务必要信息保留与监督信号设计；但属机器人动作策略而非推理型 VLM，迁移可行性尚不确定。
